To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 4-Ghz all-digital fractional-n phase-locked loop is presented with a low power TDC operating at retimed reference clocks and phase-error compensation.
a 4 GHz ADPLL has been designed and implemented in TSMC 65 nm CMOS.
the ADPLL achieves 4 GHz clock generation with 9.6mW power consumption and 97dBc phase noise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a low-power all-digital PLL for high-speed applications.
the development of an all-digital PLL for high-speed clock generation.
the development of a 4-Ghz all digital phase locked loop (ADPLL) for a 60GHz wireless communication system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented ADPLL has a good performance, a low power consumption, and a small area.
the ADPLL presented here achieves the best performance in terms of phase noise, jitter, settling time, and power consumption among the state-of-the-art all-digital PLLs.
the proposed ADPLL is the first to demonstrate a 4-Ghz fractional-N ADPLL with low-power TDC, phase-error compensator, and loop settling monitor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ADPLL is the first all digital PLL to operate at 4 GHz with a low-power fractional TDC and phase-error compensation.

the ADPLL is the first all-digital fractional-n PLL with a low power TDC operating at a retimed reference clocks and a compensator preventing phase error downfalls, and that the ADPLL achieves a low in-band phase noise and a low integrated noise with fast settling time.
the proposed ADPLL achieves the best performance among the published ADPLLs in 65 nm CMOS technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we propose a novel fractional-N PLL architecture with low-power TDC and a phase-error compensator.
the ADPLL achieves the best in-band phase noise and integrated noise among the ADPLLs operating at 4-GHz clock rates, while consuming the lowest power.
the proposed low-power TDC, the phase-error compensator, and the loop-settling monitoring scheme can be applied to a wide range of high-frequency ADPLLs with a low-rate retimed clock.
